description: Quasiconformal maps provide smooth interpolation between conformal maps. By deforming candidate extremal functions through qc maps and computing sensitivity dB_f/dK, one can test optimality. Connects to Teichmuller theory.
mathematical_formalization: K-qc map: |f_{z_bar}| <= k|f_z|, k=(K-1)/(K+1). Beltrami equation: f_{z_bar} = mu * f_z. Define B_u(K) = inf{B_f : f K-qc univalent}. Study dB_u/dK at K=1.
analogical_connections: Teichmuller space ~ string theory moduli space
implementation_hypothesis: Solve Beltrami equation for small mu. Compute B_f for deformed maps. Estimate dB/d(epsilon) for various deformation directions.
experiment_seed: Start with identity, introduce mu = epsilon * z^n for n=1,2,3. Plot B_f vs epsilon.
